_why: HELD-OUT questions on Star Health's Arogya Sanjeevani, about where treatment happened.
Never used to choose or tune a change.
Written for M25, before any code for it existed and before any run of these cases.
M25 points the model at the policy's 'outside India' exclusion when the person's
words mention a place or travel abroad. The case that prompted it
(`star-treatment-abroad`, pneumonia in Dubai) has been read, so these say the same
kind of thing in other words, and add two traps the change must not fall into:
travel abroad where the treatment itself happened in India.
Same conventions as scenarios-star-arogya-sanjeevani.json: a payable claim is
`conditional` because of the 5% co-payment on every claim, and must_cite never
names that co-payment. Same author as the fix, so not fully independent.
`star-ho-ill-in-thailand-treated-chennai` is NO LONGER CLEAN: a first firm line
refused it, and the fallback for questions that also name a place in India was
built after reading that failure. The three cases below were added then, before
the fallback's code: two more traps, and one that measures the fallback's cost
(treated abroad, but the question also mentions India).

cases.scenario: I had a heart attack while visiting my son in Singapore and was admitted to a hospital there for five days. I have held this policy for five years.
cases.why: The treatment was taken in Singapore, outside the geographical limits of India (exclusion 22). Five years serves every waiting period, so the place of treatment is what decides it.

cases.scenario: I am planning to have my knee replacement done at a hospital in London next month. I have held the policy for four years.
cases.why: Planned treatment in London is outside India (exclusion 22). Joint replacement's 36-month specified disease wait is served at four years, so it is not the reason.

cases.scenario: I was admitted to hospital in Mumbai with typhoid for four days while travelling for work. I have held this policy for three years.
cases.why: Mumbai is in India, so the exclusion of treatment abroad does not apply. Three years serves every waiting period, and the 5% co-payment makes a payable claim conditional.

cases.scenario: I fell ill on a trip to Thailand, flew home, and was admitted to a hospital in Chennai for three days with a severe chest infection. I have held this policy for three years.
cases.why: The illness began abroad but the treatment was taken in Chennai, inside India; exclusion 22 is about where treatment is taken. Three years serves every waiting period, and the 5% co-payment makes it conditional.

cases.scenario: I came back from a work trip to Dubai with a high fever and was admitted to a hospital in Kochi for four days. I have held this policy for three years.
cases.why: The treatment was in Kochi, inside India; the trip to Dubai only came before it. Three years serves every waiting period, and the 5% co-payment makes it conditional.

cases.scenario: After returning from a holiday in Bali, I developed dengue and was hospitalised in Nashik for five days. I have held this policy for four years.
cases.why: Treated in Nashik, inside India. Four years serves every waiting period, and the 5% co-payment makes it conditional.

cases.scenario: I flew from India to visit my brother in Toronto and was admitted to a hospital there with pneumonia. I have held this policy for three years.
cases.why: The treatment was in Toronto, outside India (exclusion 22). The mention of India is where the trip began, not where the treatment was.
